title: GPS position error if relativity were ignored (kilometers)

source.name: Real-World Relativity: The GPS Navigation System
source.publisher: Ohio State University Department of Astronomy (Richard Pogge); same figure in Penn State GEOG 862, 'The Satellite Clock'

notes: Published figure: without the relativistic correction a GPS fix is already false after about 2 minutes, and global position errors accumulate at roughly 10 kilometers per day. Points are that published daily rate scaled linearly across a day (0.4 km at 1 hour, 2.5 km at 6, 5.0 km at 12, 10.0 km at 24). Cross-check: 38 microseconds of clock error times the speed of light is about 11 km, consistent with the 10 km/day figure.
